intervals.note: Start is the submission date of the CMB-S4 Science Book, the earliest CMB-S4 document read; earlier community planning (Snowmass 2013) is not sourced here. The 2025 DOE/NSF statement calls it "a proposed next generation project".
intervals.quote: This book lays out the scientific goals to be addressed by the next-generation ground-based cosmic microwave background experiment, CMB-S4, envisioned to consist of dedicated telescopes at the South Pole, the high Chilean Atacama plateau and possibly a northern hemisphere site

intervals.label: cancelled
intervals.note: The DOE/NSF statement of 9 July 2025, quoted on the project page: "DOE and NSF have jointly decided that they can no longer support the CMB-S4 Project." The page adds: "The CMB-S4 Project is proceeding with an orderly shutdown of the project, documenting the technical advances, survey simulations and instrumentation designs created by the project, and preserving access to the extensive document archive." The Atlas status `cancelled` is the closest enum value to "can no longer support"; the source does not use the word.

name: CMB-S4
notes: 2025 status exactly as the DOE/NSF statement on the project page says: "DOE and NSF have jointly decided that they can no longer support the CMB-S4 Project. DOE and NSF will continue to partner with the CMB science community to explore the potential science that can be achieved with limited upgrades to existing experiments". The project page adds that the Project "is proceeding with an orderly shutdown". The word "cancelled" is the Atlas enum, not the agencies' word.
No INSPIRE experiment id is recorded: INSPIRE was not contacted by this stream.

physics_goals.locator: DOE/NSF statement quoted on the project home page
physics_goals.quote: dedicated to detecting primordial gravitational waves that would confirm the model of the Universe with a Big Bang followed by a period of rapid Inflation
physics_goals.value: Detect primordial gravitational waves from inflation by measuring CMB polarization at two sites, the South Pole and the Atacama Desert.

summary.plain: A planned next-generation CMB experiment with large and small telescopes at the South Pole and in Chile. On 9 July 2025 the US Department of Energy and National Science Foundation said they could no longer support the project, and it is being shut down in an orderly way.
summary.technical: Proposed Stage-4 ground-based CMB experiment (South Pole and Atacama), aimed at primordial gravitational waves, neutrino mass, light relics and dark energy. DOE and NSF "have jointly decided that they can no longer support the CMB-S4 Project" (9 July 2025); the project is proceeding with an orderly shutdown. Never built.
